scope.priority: OLE2 and OOXML remain the active priority; ODF deferred; iWork excluded.
scope.baseline_stage: change 0565 applied; the design is frozen in docs/performance/0566-xls-worksheet-window-design.md

hypothesis.statement: WorksheetScan reads one four-byte header per record and one read per consumed payload through a stream cursor, so change 0564 measured 266 positional reads beyond the open for a one-cell query: 177 headers, 88 payloads and one shared-string fetch.
hypothesis.mechanism: Replace the per-record scratch buffer with a retained window buffer filled by one cursor read per fill, sized 512 bytes doubling to a 64 KiB cap. Unlike change 0565's globals scan, the upper bound is exact before the scan begins because validate_sheet_offsets runs at open, so every fill is clamped to the selected sheet's own validated region and there is no spill-and-truncate. A skipped payload that extends past the filled end is passed by seeking, not by reading.
hypothesis.density_gate: Before each fill, if the mean framed bytes per record exceeds 1 KiB the fill is exact and the window target resets. Without it a sheet of large opaque records inverts the trade: a simulated 200-record opaque sheet goes from 824 bytes read to 1,613,496.
hypothesis.predicted_effect: one-cell scan reads fall from 266 to about 8 and a 16-sheet text scan from 5,277 to about 778, at roughly 22 and 17 times the bytes; source observations fall with the reads; open and list are unchanged, which is the control.

accepted_contract_changes: A skipped payload is never framed, interpreted or published, and no read begins at an offset inside one; when it extends past the filled end the scan advances past the remainder without reading it. Bytes of a skipped payload inside a window already filled to frame earlier records are read, bounded by the window ceiling and confined to the selected sheet's validated region.
An oversized record is refused on its header alone; no read is issued for its payload and no window grows to cover it.

max_worksheet_scan_bytes becomes a true read fence: no byte at or past sheet.start plus the limit is read. This is strictly tighter than today's limit-plus-four. When fewer than four bytes of budget remain the reported observed value becomes scanned_bytes plus four rather than scanned_bytes plus the frame length.
Source observations fall from one per read to one per fill; the query-level bracket is unchanged.
Within one fill, an I/O or SourceChanged failure at a later offset is reported before a framing, limit or parse error of an earlier record.

Cancellation keeps every existing check site, so the CPU interval between checks stays at one record; only the I/O interval grows to one fill, for which materialize_eager's documented 64 KiB interval on the same owner is precedent.

acceptance.primary_gate: counted-read tests must show reads disjoint and inside the selected sheet's validated region, no read issued for a skipped or oversized payload, no byte read at or past the byte limit, and the density fallback; each must fail without the change.
acceptance.secondary_gate: per-selector pread64 and statx isolated by differencing strace -f -c at 1 and 11 samples; open and list must be unchanged, which is the control proving the delta is the scan.
acceptance.byte_gate: logical bytes read per selector recorded before and after, with the increase stated explicitly rather than omitted.
acceptance.opaque_gate: re-run on the comments-opaque-heavy corpus; reads must fall or hold and bytes must not exceed today plus one window per sheet, or the density gate is unvalidated.
acceptance.latency_gate: paired A1/B1/B2/A2 p50 over the ten XLS selectors, warmup 5 and 60 samples per child, CPU pinned and ASLR disabled; cells adverse in both directions by more than 5% reported explicitly, and nanosecond-scale cells reported as below clock resolution.
acceptance.correctness_gate: full litchi-xls suite, clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied, no-default-features, fmt, and the wider OLE2 and facade suites with --no-fail-fast before commit.

cpu.aslr: disabled with setarch -R for the selector matrix

noise_floor: change 0565 measured this host's A/A drift at +1.7% to +3.2% p50 and +11.0% p99 with one binary against itself at 20 samples; tail movements below roughly 10% carry no information unless both directions agree.
